Chapter 7: The Unlikely Teachers Along the Way
Sometimes, the most powerful lessons show up in places we’d never expect. You know, faith isn’t just something we build from sermons or sacred texts. It’s shaped by the everyday people who cross our paths—each carrying their own story, their own bits of wisdom, and their own journey through struggle and hope.
Think about the neighbor who always finds something kind to say, even on those days when the world feels heavy. Or the friend who brings you soup when you’re under the weather. Maybe it’s a stranger who flashes a warm smile at the grocery store checkout, just when you need it most. These little acts of kindness, they often slip by unnoticed, but in moments of despair, they’re like lifelines. They remind us we’re not alone, and that goodness is everywhere—sometimes in the most unlikely places.
Picture this: one afternoon, a woman sits quietly in a recovery meeting. She’s listening to a man share his story, one filled with setbacks and redemption. His words aren’t polished, but they’re honest and real. No show, no pretending—just the truth, spoken straight from the heart. And in that moment, it hits her—wisdom doesn’t belong only to scholars or saints. So often, our best teachers are the people who’ve walked through fire and made it out the other side, maybe a little scarred, but still standing.
And what about children? They might surprise you as some of the most unexpected guides. Their questions are fearless and direct, and their faith is pure—not tangled up in doubt or cynicism. A simple prayer whispered before bedtime can carry more meaning than a thousand sermons. The way kids forgive so easily and love without holding back? That’s a lesson in living with an open heart.
Even the tough people in our lives—the ones who test our patience, who seem to know exactly how to push our buttons—they’re teachers, too. They show us where we’re still clinging to anger or pride, or the parts of ourselves that need a little healing. Learning to love the hard-to-love? That’s where we start to understand what grace is really about.
Over time, you start to see it: everyone’s a teacher, and every encounter is a chance to learn something new. The journey of faith isn’t something we walk alone. It’s shaped by the people we meet along the way, each one leaving a mark, each one helping us see the world—and ourselves—a little more clearly.
